subject: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — co-term options & pricing path
messages:
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@healthtech.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — co-term options & pricing path

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the open discussion yesterday. Per our call, I put together two pragmatic paths to get HealthTech both the mid-contract capacity you need for Q4 burst traffic and alignment on the renewal that co-terms to 12/31/27: a staged top-up (fast) and a consolidated co-term amendment (preferred for predictability). I attached the usage summary we referenced and an updated quote (redwood_pricing_quote_v3.pdf).

Quick highlights:
- Staged top-up: immediate capacity + one-off credit structure; aligns billing to existing term (lower immediate commitment).
- Co-term amendment: annualized uplift that moves you to calendar-year co-term with a modest volume discount at the new committed level.

Can you confirm which path you want us to price in detail? If you prefer, we can sketch a blended hybrid (top-up now, commit to co-term at renewal with ramp metrics).

Next steps I suggest:
1) You tell us preferred path by EOD Thu (6 Aug).
2) We produce final SOW + redlineable amendment and send for procurement review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call with Marcus and Tessa if useful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026_Q2_usage_summary.csv (csv), redwood_pricing_quote_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@healthtech.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Martin Sloane <martin.sloane@healthtech.com>, HealthTech Procurement <procurement@healthtech.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract capacity bump — co-term options & pricing path

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We ran the numbers and have two asks before we can move to a formal amendment:
1) Can you show the blended hybrid (top-up this quarter, then annualize at co-term) with a 10% uplift discount at the committed level? That helps us keep unit economics stable.
2) Procurement wants to keep invoice timing monthly but have the annualized commitment reflected purely as a billing anchor (no prepayment).

If you can share a concrete quote with those constraints and the delta to our existing renewal terms, Procurement will review it on Monday (10 Aug). If agreeable, Martin can sign off operationally; procurement will do legal and PO.

Thanks — Dana
Head of ML Platform
HealthTech Labs

Team —

I've modeled the blended hybrid with a 10% uplift discount. Summary:
- Incremental margin hit is ~6% at the proposed uplift level because monthly invoicing increases working capital but we keep linear unit pricing.
- If we include a 60-day ramp clause (apply discount once usage stabilizes above threshold for 60 days) we mitigate short-term churn risk.
- Approve discount with two guardrails: 1) SLA fallback to standard routing after sustained >30% over-commit burst; 2) commit review at 6 months to re-evaluate uplift sizing.

If Marcus and Kim approve, Legal can draft a co-term amendment + SOW; I can sign off on the finance memo for discounts.

Rishi
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference
